title: Towards a Densing Law for User Representation Learning at Billion-Scale Capacity
abstract: arXiv:2608.23392v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: User representation learning in real-world industrial scenarios is commonly scaled by increasing user amount, behavioral sequence length and model size. However, existing methods face two challenges: (i) Bottleneck for raw data scaling at billion-scale capacity, as performance exhibit diminishing performance gains with larger-scale raw text user behavioral input, which can be mitigated by tokenization. (ii) Lack of quantitative analysis of how tokenization configurations should scale with data size. In this report, we propose User Behavioral Densing Law for characterizing the quantitative relationship between data scale and the minimum sufficient tokenization capacity. Firstly, we conduct a pilot study on raw & tokenized scaling comparison on billion-scale Alipay dataset, revealing the raw data scaling bottleneck and the sustained gains enabled by tokenization. To derive the scaling pattern governing the minimum sufficient tokenization

translated_title: 迈向十亿级容量下用户表征学习的稠密化定律
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.23392v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：在真实工业场景中，用户表征学习通常通过增加用户数量、行为序列长度和模型规模来扩展。然而，现有方法面临两个挑战：（i）在十亿级容量下原始数据扩展的瓶颈，因为随着更大规模的原始文本用户行为输入，性能提升逐渐减弱，这可以通过分词化来缓解。（ii）缺乏对分词配置应如何随数据规模扩展的定量分析。在本报告中，我们提出了用户行为稠密化定律，用于刻画数据规模与最小充分分词容量之间的定量关系。首先，我们在十亿级支付宝数据集上进行了原始与分词化扩展对比的初步研究，揭示了原始数据扩展的瓶颈以及分词化带来的持续收益。为了推导出支配最小充分分词化的扩展模式...
tldr: 本论文提出了“用户行为稠密化定律”，量化了数据规模与最小充分分词容量之间的关系，解决了十亿级场景下原始数据扩展瓶颈和分词配置扩展缺乏定量分析的问题。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a "User Behavioral Densing Law" to quantify the relationship between data scale and minimum sufficient tokenization capacity, addressing the raw data scaling bottleneck and the lack of quantitative analysis on tokenization scaling in billion-scale scenarios.
